w: Swamishri departed from Wellingborough at 10.40 am and arrived at Dollis Hill, London at 12.55pm. On entering Arvindbhai Guru's home, Swamishri fondly recalled the memories of Yogiji Maharaj's stay here in 1970.

Kishore - Kishori National Convention During the morning session, kishores and kishoris explored one of the most important aspects of society – education. Panel discussions, featuring successful college students and graduates, along with lively skits and enlightening speeches from sadhus highlighted the importance and necessity of hard work in education. Doctor Swami also offered valuable guidance on how to create a balance between education and satsang. After listening to a debate about the pros and cons of going away from home to attend college, Swamishri offered his blessings, saying that no matter where one studies, one should be able to keep God and His holy Sadhu with him by abiding by their every wish. In a special Guru Purnima evening programme, sadhus recounted personal incidents of Swamishri's love expressed towards them. The entire programme was organised around the kirtan, ‘Sant vinã re sãchi kon kahe...’ which describes the guru as being the only person capable of offering true bliss. Swamishri was asked to explain how one can please one's guru, and he explained in his blessings that one must keep the company of the guru with no expectations, and readily accept any seva given by him.
Finally, Swamishri sprayed coloured water on his beloved Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. Thereafter, kishores joyously danced to kirtans as they were sprayed with the sanctified water.
The evening assembly in the presence of Swamishri was held as the symbolic celebration of the Rath Yatra festival.
The murtis of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj were seated in a decorated, motorised chariot and was manoeuvered around the assembly hall. In conclusion, Swamishri performed the Rath Yatra celebration arti.
In the mandir sanctum the wooden murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj was reformed by expert craftsmen. Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of the murti .

ds.t: A simple way out of addiction
w: A youth had come for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He was not wearing a kanthi around his neck. Swamishri asked him the reason.
"I do not want to dishonour the kanthi," the youth said hesitantly.
Swamishri said, "Why? Do you have some addiction or vice?"
"I do."
"Then give it up. If you wear the kanthi, you will get strength," Swamishri said.
"It is not that much of a vice, but basically I have to go out of town and cannot keep my vows, so I feel this way."

Swamishri said, "You have to go out of town, but does that mean you must smoke bidis and cigarettes? One should stay away from addiction; only then will one be happy. So give up the addiction, and if you wear the kanthi you will have strength and everything will go." In this way Swamishri lovingly made him give up his addiction and take refuge in God.

w: A youth had come for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. There was no kanthi on his neck. Swamishri asked him the reason for this.

Swamishri said, "You may have to travel out of town, but does that mean you have to smoke bidis and cigarettes? One should stay away from addiction altogether; only then can one be happy. So give up the addiction, and if you wear the kanthi you will have strength and everything will be given up." In this way, lovingly freeing him from his addiction, Swamishri made him take God's refuge.

Prior to his morning puja, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of murtis for the BAPS hari mandir in Wellingborough (UK). Swamishri performed his puja in his room.

The Guru Purnima assembly had commenced at 8.30 am. Satyaprakash Swami, Viveksagar Swami, Tyagvallabh Swami, Dr Swami and Mahant Swami spoke about the glory of Swamishri’s life and works. More than 60,000 devotees from all over India and abroad had gathered for Swamishri’s darshan. Stage guests Shri Ravichandran, director of IIM, Indore, Shri B.G. Patel, Vice-Chancellor of Sardar Patel University and Shri C.L. Patel, Chairman of Charutar Vidya Mandal, were honoured with garlands by senior sadhus.

Swamishri inaugurated an Mp3 and audio CD of Gunatitanand Swami’s biography (Gujarati), a CD on Swaminarayan dhun, ‘Naam Smaran’, a foot high murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni and a set of moral stories for students, ‘Sucharitam’, written by Sadhu Priyadarshandas. Thereafter, Swamishri was honoured with a variety of garlands by senior sadhus. A traditional dance on the lyric “Swaminarayan Charankamalma…” was beautifully performed by BAPS children of Mogri centre. Then a pushpanjali ritual was performed by all to offer respect to Shriji Maharaj and Swamishri. The celebration climaxed with Swamishri’s blessings, “Today is the best of days for the whole world. Through the guru one attains spiritual knowledge and then liberation. Veda Vyas has mentioned this in the Vedas, Upanishads. Gita and Shrimad Bhagvat. Shriji Maharaj has revealed in the Vachanamrut and Gunatitanand Swami has expressed in his Swamini Vato that by taking refuge in a guru one becomes free from all bondage. By going to him one becomes liberated from maya, samsara, I-ness and Mine-ness and subsequently one becomes happy. The more one consolidates the knowledge of atma-Paramatma in one’s life the more happiness and peace one experiences in life.”After the celebration devotees were served maha-prasad.

st.t: President of India, Her Excellency Pratibha Patil, Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir
w: Her Excellency President Patil and her husband, Dr D.R. Shekhawat, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham this morning, in commemoration of their 44th wedding anniversary and Guru Purnima. Their daughter, Smt. Jyoti Rathore, and son, Sh Smt. Jyoti Rathore, and ri Rajendra Singh, also accompanied them on this special occasion. They were traditionally welcomed by Dr J.M. Dave on behalf of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the inspirer of Swaminarayan Akshardham and the head of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

The President and her family offered prayers and flowers to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Ganeshji and Hanumanji. Thereafter, they visited the entire Akshardham complex, which included the Ten Gates, Bhakti Dwar, Mayur Dwar, Holy Footprints, Elephant Plinth and Narayan Sarovar, which contains water from 151 holy rivers across India.
The family then performed ‘Abhishek’ – the ceremony of pouring holy water on the sacred murti of Bhagwan Neelkanth.
Thereafter, the President and her family visited the Hall of Values exhibition, the Giant Screen show and the spectacular boat ride exhibition portraying Indian culture.

Sharing her experience in the opinion book at Swaminarayan Akshardham, she wrote: “Today, on the very sacred Guru Purnima day we had the great fortune to have darshan and offer our homage to Bhagwan Swaminarayan. We thoroughly enjoyed every show. The life, penance, and challenges of Shri Swaminarayan tell us about his tremendous spiritual strength. I congratulate each and everyone who had contributed to this extraordinary monument. This creation was due to the inspiration of Pramukh Swamiji, who is worthy of praise by the nation.”
In honour of her memorial visit, President Patil and family were gifted Akshardham mementos.
In all, the President and her family enjoyed the two-and-a-half hour visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham.

ds.t: The Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj met Prem Kumar Dhumal, the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, and Kisan Kumar, the Deputy Chief Minister. Kisan Kumar is a satsangi. Moreover, he has great faith in the abhishek of Nilkanth Varni here.

Swamishri honoured both dignitaries by placing garlands on them. Prem Kumar Dhumal spoke about some special features of Himachal Pradesh and, speaking of his own experience, said, "I first had the good fortune of your darshan in Gandhinagar. When I came for your darshan, you asked whether my problem had been resolved. At that time there really was some political problem in Himachal Pradesh. But when I came out after taking your blessings, the news came that the problem had been resolved."

Vedmangal Swami, who had come from Jaipur, spoke about the particular traits of the devotees of Jaipur. He said, "There is a lot of superstition among everyone there. As soon as they come to the mandir, they say, 'Do you read palms?'"
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Tell everyone that they should keep their connection with God and do devotion to God."

ds.t: The Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj met Premkumar Dhumal, Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, and Deputy Chief Minister Kisankumar. Kisankumar is a satsangi. Moreover, he has great faith in the abhishek of Nilkanth Varni here.

Swamishri honoured both dignitaries by placing garlands on them. Premkumar Dhumal spoke of some special features of Himachal Pradesh and, telling of his own experience, said, "The first time I had the good fortune of your darshan was in Gandhinagar. When I came for your darshan, you asked whether my problem had been solved, and truly there was a political problem in Himachal Pradesh at that time. But when I came out after receiving your blessings, the news came that the problem had been solved."

Vedmangal Swami, who had come from Jaipur, spoke about the particular ways of the devotees of Jaipur. He said, "There is a lot of superstition among everyone there. As soon as they come to the mandir, they immediately say, 'Do you read palms?'"
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Tell everyone that they should keep their union with Bhagwan and do devotion to Bhagwan."
Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj came before the shrine of Ghanshyam Maharaj, he called the pujari, Rujuswarupdas Swami, and said, "The turban is not black."
Rujuswarupdas Swami said, "Swami! It is dark blue. We will change it."

The turban was such a dark blue that at first glance one would not notice it, but Swamishri's subtle eye of devotion noticed it immediately and expressed his wish: the clothes are black, so the turban too should be black to match.

As Mahant Swami Maharaj was coming out of the pujari's storeroom, the youths doing seva showed Swamishri a picture of a heart and asked, "You have kept a place for us in your heart, but what should we do so that you have a place in our hearts?"
Swamishri said, "Commands."

As he was entering the sadhus' ashram, a young man standing there made a gesture with both hands meaning "May I have a very firm bond, a love, with you." Swamishri said, "Commands." That is, the way to have firm love for Swamishri is to follow his commands.

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj sat in his room for his meal, he gave prasad to the local sadhus with his own hands. Gunvatsaldas Swami went to give him a wet tissue to wipe his soiled hands. Swamishri said no... Then he himself explained the reason: "Then every time you will give me only tissues, and then everyone else who sees it will also give only tissues."
What subtle thrift! What deep thinking!! The great sadhu is not only the bearer of the spiritual virtues described in the scriptures, he holds every virtue known on earth.

ds.t: The flower that was not there
w: Today, since Mahant Swami Maharaj was going to Chicago, he came to the mandir for darshan in the evening too. A knot had been tied in Yogi Bapa's upper cloth. Pointing to the beautiful flower placed on it, he said, "It was not there in the morning."
Everyone was astonished: "With what concentration Swamishri has darshan!"

Mahant Swami Maharaj got into the car and left for the airport. In the car was Oscar, the Mexican security officer who had served with great enthusiasm, always on his feet, for 17 days. Swamishri was moved by his seva and, addressing him, said, "Akshardham!" That is, he gave him Akshardham!
What a great reward for serving wholeheartedly for 17 days!

Just as Shriji Maharaj gave a great reward for even a little seva to Bibadi of Bhal or the courtesan of Jetalpur, the same Shriji Maharaj today, in the form of the sadhu, showered his grace on Oscar too.

ds.t: Do your best, leave the rest
w: Mahant Swami Maharaj came by car from the airport to the Chicago mandir premises. Receiving the welcome, he came to the podium of the mandir. Giving his blessings, Swamishri said, "Jai Shri Swaminarayan. Shriji Maharaj says, 'To see divinity in everyone is itself brahmavidya (the knowledge of Brahman).' Ego, jealousy, all of it is rubbish. Setting it aside, not just setting it aside but crushing it: 'Do your best, leave the rest.'"

The place was the podium of the mandir and the time was the welcome. Even at such a time and in such a place, Swamishri spoke about "seeing divinity." How much this sense of divinity must be playing in his heart!
